croton-mammy: Croton 'Mammy' twists and curls its leaves — no two leaves on the plant share the same shape.
alocasia-amazonica: Alocasia Amazonica was bred in Miami, not the Amazon — the name is pure marketing, and it stuck worldwide.
philedendron-birkin: Philodendron Birkin appeared as a random mutation on a nursery bench — every Birkin in the world descends from that one plant.
dracaena-darasingh-plant: Named after the wrestler 'Dara Singh', this Dracaena is known for its broad, strong leaves.
zamia-zz-small: The ZZ plant survives weeks of neglect by storing water in rhizomes underground — it's practically a succulent in disguise.
ficus-macolame: Ficus 'Alii' has narrow leaves like a willow — a fig that behaves like a graceful indoor tree.
singonium-green: Arrowhead plants start with arrow leaves and later grow divided, hand-shaped ones — same plant, two silhouettes.
jade-plant-m: Jade plants can live for decades — some family heirloom jades in India are older than the houses they sit in.
draceana-dara-singh-m: This bold Dracaena was named after wrestler Dara Singh — for its broad, strong-looking leaves.
zamia-plant-zz-big: ZZ plants tolerate low light so well that mall use them in windowless corridors — they survive on fluorescent light alone.
verigated-jade-mini-indorenursery: Variegation — the white edges on this jade — is a natural mutation, and variegated plants grow slower because white patches can't photosynthesise.
hanging-crasula-ovata: Trailing jade's leaves are tiny water tanks — a plump leaf means the plant is perfectly watered.
moon-cactus: A moon cactus is two cacti grafted into one — the colourful top can't make its own food and lives on the green base below.
echivera-gibbiflora-dc: Echeveria rosettes turn from green to pink under bright sun — the colour is a natural sunscreen the plant produces.
haworthia-limifolia: Haworthia leaves have translucent 'windows' at their tips — they let sunlight deep inside the leaf while the plant sits buried.
